subject.title: fix(qa): reject runtime tool intent without result evidence

question: Should release validation intentionally require only `session-status`, `web-fetch`, and `web-search` until the nine report-only runtime-tool paths have real linked product-result fixtures?
rationale: The implementation correctly prevents false-positive coverage, but choosing which tools remain release-required is a QA policy and release-assurance decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Accept the result-backed minimum
options.body: Merge with the three required rows and retain the demoted rows as explicit report-only gaps until each has real product-result evidence.

options.title: Keep more rows required
options.body: Require new or repaired fixtures that capture linked successful product results before retaining any additional runtime-tool row as release-required.

options.title: Split policy from mechanism
options.body: Land only the per-cell status and successful-result enforcement, then decide required-row metadata in a separately owner-approved change.

recommendation.title: Accept the result-backed minimum
recommendation.body: Merge with the three required rows and retain the demoted rows as explicit report-only gaps until each has real product-result evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged QA runtime-pair and suite-runner work places this decision closest to their current area context.
